_readme: Knobs for the Claude Code signaller. Edit freely; no rebuild step. Run `pwsh scripts/install.ps1 -Test` to preview every signal.

done._when: Claude finished a turn and handed control back to you.
done._minTurnSeconds: Stay silent for turns shorter than this. The single best noise filter: it kills the 'ok, done' chatter and only speaks up for work you actually walked away from.

needsInput._when: Claude is blocked on you: a permission prompt, or an agent asking a question. You are the bottleneck, so this always fires.

idle._when: Fires ~60s after Claude stopped and you still have not come back. The escalation rung: this is the one that means you genuinely walked away, so it is the one wired to phone push.

failed._when: The turn died on an API error (rate limit, overload, auth).

events._sound: Any ms-winsoundevent name: Notification.Default, .IM, .Mail, .Reminder, .SMS, .Looping.Alarm, .Looping.Call. Empty string for a silent toast.
events._speak: Read a short summary of what Claude said out loud, via the built-in Windows voice. No API key, no network.
events._push: Send it to your phone. Requires the push block below.

_whenFocused: silent = say nothing when you are already looking at the Claude window. full = notify regardless.
_focusPattern: Case-insensitive regex matched against the foreground window title. Claude Code sets the terminal title, so this can distinguish tabs, not just apps. Run `scripts/install.ps1 -WhoHasFocus` to see the live title and tune this.
_cooldownMs: Swallow a second signal fired within this window, so overlapping events do not stack.

toast._aumid: Borrowing Claude Desktop's app id is what gets you the real Claude icon and name on the toast instead of a generic PowerShell one. If Claude Desktop is not installed, the toast falls back to a system sound.
toast._bodyMaxChars: How much of Claude's closing message to show. It is stripped of code fences and markdown first.

speech._maxWords: Speech is a headline, not a readout. Keep it short.

push._enabled: Turn on, then set ntfyTopic to any hard-to-guess string, e.g. claude-a7f3k9x2. Install the ntfy app on your phone and subscribe to that exact topic. No account, no key.
push._warning: ntfy.sh topics are public to anyone who guesses the name, and the body contains Claude's closing message. Pick a long random topic, or self-host and change server.
